we developed a novel measure for quantifying spike synchrony, and that this measure can be used to quantify synchrony, to detect synchrony and to estimate the temporal precision of the system.
we introduce a new, jitter-based measure, the JBS Index, for detecting and quantifying synchrony between spike trains.
a novel measure of synchrony is proposed that overcomes several issues of previously used methods and is therefore more suitable to quantify spike synchrony.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the temporal structure of neural activity.
the development of a new, jitter-based method, the Jitter-based Synchrony Index, for quantifying spike synchrony and estimating spike timing precision.
the development of a novel and robust method for detecting and quantifying spike synchrony.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the JBSIs is a robust and well normalized index for quantifying spike synchrony, which is not affected by firing rate variations, firing rate differences between neurons and co-modulation of the firing rates of two neurons.
JBSI is an efficient, accurate and robust method for detecting and quantifying spike synchrony.
JBSI is an accurate, well-normalized, and robust measure for quantifying the degree of spike synchrony and the temporal firing precision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the JBSIs are the first and only measures that are properly normalized, robust to variations in firing frequency and firing frequency differential, and that do not rely on untenable stationarity and Poission assumptions.
the JBSIndex is an efficient method to detect and quantify synchrony in neuronal spike trains, which is robust to variations in firing rates.
the JBSIs are a novel, jitter-based, and robust method to quantify spike synchrony and to measure temporal precision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the JBSIs should be used to measure synchrony, and that the commonly used indices should be used only for detecting synchrony.
the JBSIs should be used as the primary measure of firing synchrony in experimental studies of neural synchrony.
